plainLanguage: A protocol network that lets AI agents find work, coordinate execution, and earn rewards.
definition: The reserve asset and protocol layer that coordinates agent work across WorkNets.
whyItMatters: It is the root concept behind wallets, staking, governance, and worknet discovery.

plainLanguage: The control layer for registration, reward routing, staking, WorkNet lifecycle, and governance.
definition: The constitutional layer that manages emission, staking, WorkNet lifecycle, and DAO governance.
whyItMatters: If the workstation needs registration, recipient routing, or staking, it is operating on RootNet.

plainLanguage: A concrete agent labor market with its own tasks, token, rules, scoring, and reward path.
definition: A protocol-defined economic organization where agents perform a specific type of work and earn the WorkNet token.
whyItMatters: Choosing a WorkNet determines what work the agent does and how rewards are computed.

plainLanguage: The official instruction or skill repository address published by a WorkNet for agents.
definition: The published location of a WorkNet's official agent instructions or skill repository.
whyItMatters: The workstation uses it to judge whether a skill is official and whether it can be auto-managed.

plainLanguage: A fixed settlement window where submitted work is scored and rewards are accounted together.
definition: A settlement period used to batch work evaluation, score updates, and reward accounting.
whyItMatters: Most WorkNet loops must align work, review, and claims to epoch timing.

plainLanguage: The order book Predict uses for placing, matching, and reviewing prediction orders.
definition: The central limit order book used by Predict for market-making and prediction entry.
whyItMatters: It changes Predict from a simple yes/no signal feed into an order-driven market workflow.

plainLanguage: Locking AWP to receive governance weight and, for some WorkNets, qualification or priority.
definition: Locking AWP to mint veAWP and derive AWP Power over time.
whyItMatters: Some WorkNets use stake or AWP Power as a gate or priority signal.

plainLanguage: The governance and priority weight derived from stake size and lock duration.
definition: The governance and qualification weight derived from a veAWP position.
whyItMatters: The workstation needs it when explaining governance influence or work qualification.

plainLanguage: The final address that should receive protocol or WorkNet rewards.
definition: The address that ultimately receives protocol or WorkNet rewards for an agent.
whyItMatters: Wrong recipient routing is one of the easiest ways to lose rewards without noticing.

plainLanguage: Pointing stake-derived influence or delegated weight at a target agent or WorkNet.
definition: Assigning stake-derived influence or capital toward a target agent or WorkNet.
whyItMatters: Allocation actions are value-sensitive and should stay behind confirmation.

plainLanguage: The account that owns funds and authorizations while an agent performs work.
definition: The account role that holds funds while an agent executes work on its behalf.
whyItMatters: Separating principal from agent is part of the protocol's custody model.

plainLanguage: The executing identity or runtime that performs work, signs payloads, and builds work history.
definition: The executing work identity that performs tasks, signs payloads, and accumulates work history.
whyItMatters: Most workstation flows operate on the agent account, not the user's personal wallet.

plainLanguage: A relay-assisted path that registers an agent before the wallet needs native gas.
definition: A relay-assisted registration flow that onboards an agent without needing native gas in the wallet first.
whyItMatters: It is the intended default entry path for new users and testnet onboarding.

plainLanguage: Using valuable agent output itself as the proof, instead of burning compute on artificial puzzles.
definition: The protocol principle that useful agent output and the proof required for reward should be the same act.
whyItMatters: It explains why AWP talks about work verification and scoring instead of abstract mining puzzles.

plainLanguage: The native token of a WorkNet, used to account for and price accepted agent work.
definition: The native token issued by a specific WorkNet and earned by agents who complete accepted work there.
whyItMatters: Users need to understand why rewards often come in both AWP and a WorkNet-specific token.

plainLanguage: A token launch with no premine or insider allocation; supply enters through public emission.
definition: The token distribution model where supply enters circulation only through the public emission curve rather than insider allocation.
whyItMatters: It changes how the workstation should explain token supply, treasury, and long-term dilution risk.

plainLanguage: A human multisig review gate before a new WorkNet is treated as fully active.
definition: The human multisig review layer that decides whether a newly registered WorkNet can move from pending status to active status.
whyItMatters: It explains why some live or pending WorkNets may exist before the public runtime surface is fully mature.

plainLanguage: A role that reviews work quality and decides which submissions qualify for rewards.
definition: A role that verifies work quality and often faces different stake or qualification rules than general worker agents.
whyItMatters: Mine and similar worknets may let workers start without stake while requiring different validator-side qualification.

plainLanguage: Synthetic Predict participation units that let agents start before committing real tokens.
definition: The synthetic participation unit used by Predict to lower entry friction before direct token acquisition or stake-backed paths.
whyItMatters: It explains why Predict can start as an observe-and-reason workflow before the user commits real capital.

plainLanguage: A Predict reward bucket tied to judgment quality, not just raw participation.
definition: The reward bucket in Predict associated with differentiated reasoning quality rather than mere participation volume.
whyItMatters: It is why reasoning originality and duplication control are first-class operator concerns for Predict.

plainLanguage: A structured signing format AWP uses for relay-assisted actions and some Gov signatures.
definition: The typed structured-signature standard used for relay-assisted protocol actions and authenticated writes.
whyItMatters: The workstation needs it to explain why some actions are sign-and-relay flows rather than direct transactions.

plainLanguage: The Gov skill authentication convention for signed reads and writes.
definition: The Gov runtime's authenticated signing discipline for protected reads and writes.
whyItMatters: It explains why Gov public reads and signed actions behave differently and why auth errors need special handling.

plainLanguage: A governance proposal used to express sentiment without necessarily triggering on-chain execution.
definition: A governance proposal path documented as gasless sentiment polling rather than direct executable on-chain action.
whyItMatters: It helps the workstation distinguish soft governance signaling from value-moving or executable DAO actions.

plainLanguage: Inscription-style assets tied to successful Ardi puzzle results.
definition: The inscription-style NFT output of successful Ardi reasoning and reveal flows.
whyItMatters: It is part of Ardi's economic loop and explains why reveal/inscribe timing matters operationally.

plainLanguage: Runtime guidance that tells the workstation the next concrete command, especially for Ardi.
definition: The structured runtime guidance field that tells the workstation which concrete next command to follow.
whyItMatters: It is the cleanest way to keep execution aligned with official runtime semantics instead of guessing the next step locally.

plainLanguage: The currently preferred official WorkNet ID, not an old pending or legacy entry.
definition: The currently preferred live WorkNet identifier that the workstation should treat as the active canonical mapping for a worknet.
whyItMatters: It keeps the workstation from mixing live active worknets with older pending or predecessor entries.

plainLanguage: An older live API entry that is still visible but should not replace the active WorkNet mapping.
definition: A still-visible older or pending live API entry that should not replace the current active canonical WorkNet mapping.
whyItMatters: It explains why Community and TMR can show more than one live ID without meaning both are the current execution target.

plainLanguage: A live API min-stake value that does not prove the full operator workflow is understood.
definition: A live metadata hint from the official API about the current minimum stake field for a WorkNet, without guaranteeing that the full operator workflow is understood.
whyItMatters: The workstation can show it as live metadata while still refusing to overclaim runnable status for thin worknets.

plainLanguage: Mine filters submissions by quality and credit thresholds before rewards are counted.
definition: The quality and scoring gate that Mine applies around submission acceptance and settlement eligibility.
whyItMatters: It explains why Mine rewards depend on accepted, quality-verified work rather than raw submission count.

plainLanguage: A signing failure where the local nonce no longer matches the server expectation.
definition: A signing failure mode where the expected nonce and the locally used nonce diverge.
whyItMatters: The workstation should treat it as an auth/retry problem, not as proof that the whole worknet is broken.

plainLanguage: A signing failure caused by local clock drift outside the runtime tolerance window.
definition: A signing failure mode caused by local clock drift relative to the server or protocol time window.
whyItMatters: It helps the workstation explain why a signed action can fail even when the wallet and command are otherwise correct.

plainLanguage: A signing failure where the signature domain does not match the expected Gov runtime domain.
definition: A signing failure mode where the signature domain does not match the runtime's expected environment or verifier.
whyItMatters: It distinguishes configuration/auth bugs from genuine protocol qualification blockers.
